desc:
image is an m x n binary picture: 1 is a black pixel and 0 is a white pixel. All the black pixels are connected to each other through horizontal and vertical neighbours, so they form a single blob (there is exactly one blob and it is not empty).

You are given the position (x, y) (row x, column y, both 0-based) of one black pixel. Return the area (number of cells) of the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that contains all the black pixels. A solution that inspects far fewer than m * n cells exists.
constraints: The black pixels form exactly one connected blob (4-directional) and image[x][y] = 1
hints: Scanning the whole picture to find the extreme black rows and columns is O(m * n). Because the blob is connected, a lot more can be said about which rows and columns contain black pixels.

Every row and column that contains a black pixel forms one unbroken range, and the given pixel (x, y) lies inside it. So going away from x, rows are either 'has black' and then 'all white' with no coming back.

Binary search each of the four borders: the first column in [0, y] containing a black pixel, the last in [y, n-1], and likewise for rows with [0, x] and [x, m-1]. Each probe scans one row or column. Multiply the resulting height and width.
editorial: Let a column be 'occupied' if it holds at least one black pixel. The blob is connected, so the occupied columns are contiguous: if columns a < c are occupied, any column between them is crossed by the path that links the two blobs parts, hence occupied too. The same holds for rows. The known pixel (x, y) is inside both contiguous ranges.

Therefore the columns in [0, y] read 'white ... white, occupied ... occupied', a monotone pattern, and the left border is the first occupied column, found by binary search. The right border is the last occupied column in [y, n-1] (pattern 'occupied ... occupied, white ... white'); the top and bottom borders are found in the same way with rows.

Each of the four searches does O(log) probes, and a probe checks one row (O(n)) or one column (O(m)), so the cost is O(m log n + n log m). The final area is (bottom - top + 1) * (right - left + 1). Without the connectivity guarantee the pattern would not be monotone and binary search would fail.
time: O(m log n + n log m)
